newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Crowd loots arms depot, rebellion creeps northward.
newsitem.headline: Crowd loots arms depot, rebellion creeps northward.

text.p: About 100 people denouncing Albanian President Sali Berisha looted automatic weapons from a depot near the town of Elbasan on Wednesday as a rebellion against the authorities crept northward towards the capital.
Reuter correspondent Giles Elgood saw the crowd surge into the depot near the town, only 55 km (40 miles) south of Tirana, and leave loaded down with Kalashnikov rifles.

"Down with Berisha!" yelled the crowd. Many demanded the return of money lost in the collapse of fraudulent investment schemes which sparked more than a month of unrest in which at least 40 people have died.
Police and Albanian secret police mounted a token guard outside the depot, located in the village of Mjeks, and fired into the air in an attempt to persuade the crowd not to take the weapons.
One man was shot in the leg, apparently by accident.

The anti-government rebels have seized control of most of southern Albania and are ignoring a deal signed last weekend by Berisha and opposition parties giving them an amnesty if they put down their weapons. The deal also provides for an all-party government and early elections.
